acceptance: CONTRIBUTING, SECURITY, SUPPORT, and CODE_OF_CONDUCT exist, are internally consistent with AGENTS.md and canonical governance, and do not invent unavailable private contact channels or guarantees.
Bug/feature issue forms and the pull-request template collect reproducibility, platform/runtime, evidence, security/privacy, provenance/license, testing, and scope information appropriate to Kernux.

Repository governance documents canonical authority order, PR-based change discipline, exact-head evidence, no evidence fabrication, donor provenance requirements, and policy-change governance without granting contributors or agents implicit authority.
README exposes the contribution/support/security/governance entry points and public security guidance explicitly avoids disclosing unpublished vulnerabilities in public issues.
The existing workspace checker fails if required community/governance surfaces disappear, and its regression tests plus the full repository baseline pass.
The WorkPacket binds exact canonical evidence that KX-P00-S01-T01 is already PROVEN; no unsupported native lifecycle state is fabricated.

Exact implementation passes YAML/Markdown structural review, focused workspace-checker tests, pnpm check, Diffcipline R1 PASS, OpenCodeReview on supported changed files, and post-merge main qualification.

minimality.rationale: Use the existing repository governance, workspace checker, GitHub-native community surfaces, and current CI; add no new package or action dependency.

requirements: Do not invent a private security email, SLA, bounty, legal entity, CLA/DCO requirement, or enforcement authority that repository truth does not establish.
Security reports must be steered away from public issues without falsely claiming a private GitHub reporting feature is enabled.
Issue and PR templates must not invite secrets, PHI, credentials, or other sensitive data into public GitHub content.
Governance must preserve canonical authority, exact-evidence requirements, donor provenance, and branch protection rather than letting templates override them.

outcome: Kernux has a complete, discoverable, repository-enforced contribution, security, support, conduct, issue, pull-request, and governance baseline before product implementation begins.
rationale: T03 is the only remaining P00 macro task. Its T01 dependency is already canonically PROVEN. The repository currently lacks the community-health files and issue/PR templates named by the master plan; this Grain establishes them without inventing private contacts or importing third-party template text.

risk.recovery: Revert the bounded governance implementation slices and closeout; no product runtime state or user data is created.

scope_in: Add original Kernux-owned CONTRIBUTING.md, SECURITY.md, SUPPORT.md, and CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md with clear scope, reporting, evidence, provenance, and conduct expectations.

Add structured bug and feature issue forms, issue-template configuration, and a pull-request template that route security reports away from public issues and require bounded evidence/provenance disclosures.

Add docs/governance/REPOSITORY_GOVERNANCE.md defining repository authority, branch/PR discipline, evidence-before-done rules, provenance boundaries, review expectations, and escalation of policy changes.
Make the community/governance baseline discoverable from README and enforce required governance paths through the existing workspace checker with regression coverage.
Bind the already-PROVEN KX-P00-S01-T01 prerequisite through exact canonical repository evidence rather than fabricating an unsupported SpecGrain lifecycle dependency.
scope_out: No CLA, DCO, legal-entity ownership claim, private maintainer email, response-time SLA, or security bounty promise is invented.
No branch-protection setting, GitHub repository setting, donor product-source import, product code, P01 contract work, release qualification, or cloud/runtime feature is changed.
Do not copy Contributor Covenant or other third-party governance templates verbatim; community text is Kernux-owned original prose unless separately admitted through provenance/notices.
